674	## Performance Implications
675	- **CPU (all UNVERIFIED on a release export; S1, S0-f, S3 pending)**: the GDD's review coefficients (5 / 10 / 15 microseconds per node / edge / compartment) give about 825 microseconds for the home ship alone and about 1.7 ms at the weld set per step; at the 0 / 2 / 4 stagger that is roughly 0.3 ms and 0.6 ms per hook, so the weld set is **at or just over the 0.5 ms share** on those coefficients, which is why S1 gates acceptance and the ladder of § 13.1 exists. The active-list indirection adds about 5 nanoseconds per element (probe (d)), the queue sorts at most 43 microseconds at the 64-entry bound (probe (c)), and a `clampi` or `mini` adds about 4 nanoseconds per call (probe (f)); `IntMath.floor_div` is about 12 times a bare operator (ADR-0005 P14). The first hook after a snapshot pays one copy-on-write per written column (about 70 columns, tens of microseconds). The eager rebuild adds O(N + E) to each structural mutator.
676	- **Memory**: the accumulators are a handful of per-compartment and per-section `PackedInt64Array`s, the active lists and the island, candidate and queue buffers are `int32` arrays of the node and edge row counts, and the descriptor store is ADR-0011's: tens of kilobytes at capacity, well under 1 MB at MVP; nothing is allocated in a phase.
677	- **Load Time**: `post_restore` is one `ensure_derived` plus the bucket seeds and the structural checks (working budget 1.1 ms of the 2 ms); M19 on wake is one O(rows) pass.
678	- **Network**: none at MVP; `SHARED_SUMMARY` (VS-B) reads the same columns.
679	
680	## Migration Plan
681	There is no Graph code yet. Implementation order: (1) `src/shared/graph/graph_rules.gd` additions (`gas_flux`, `gate_floor`, `apply_loss`, `rng_subject`, `rng_counter`, `burst_hit`, `onset_valid`, `alarm_capable`) with their unit tests and golden counter vectors; (2) the S1 stub Graph: the three hooks and twelve empty phases over the real active lists and accumulators on a synthetic F-MVP-sized fixture, plus the benchmark harness and `WorkCounter` hookup, so the ladder decision is made before the phase bodies are written; (3) `ensure_derived` with the connectivity predicate, components and trees, active lists and the head guard, with the late-rebuild assertion; (4) the hook skeleton, cursors and `HOOK_CURSOR`; (5) the phases in order 0 to 11, each landing with its D.15 fixture and its write-set test; (6) the queue enqueue and drain, then the mutators; (7) dormancy and the M19 re-basing; (8) the RE-1 to RE-3 restore-equivalence tests. The Foundation Asks and the GDD syncs below land before the stories that depend on them. No existing code or save format is migrated.
682	
683	## Validation Criteria
684	- **Registration and cursors:** three descriptors with divisor `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, offsets 0 / 2 / 4, both edges `tolerates_stale`, an empty boot-warning list, and a golden test of the relative order of the Graph hooks and their neighbours (Risk 7); `step_no` equal for the three hooks with `ClockView.tick()` at T and at T+1; a replayed hook, a regressed clock and the step-0 exception behave as § 1 says.
685	- **Phase order and write sets:** a trace test shows phases 0 to 11 in order each step; for every phase, a column-diff harness runs it alone over each fixture and asserts the set of changed persisted columns is within the phase's declared write set and the discipline (JAC / ALLOC / OWN) declared in its doc comment.
686	- **Scratch hygiene:** every accumulator is all-zero at every hook exit on every fixture; `late_rebuilds` is 0; `saturations` is all zeros.

116: pure, stateless, shared:  IntMath (lsr, floor_div, ceil_div, posmod_i, low32)   Ihash (63-bit, presentation and non-RNG variation)   Hex64
142:1. **Default: the helpers.** In `src/sim/**` and `src/kernel/**`, division and modulus go through `IntMath.floor_div(a, b)`, `IntMath.ceil_div(a, b)` and `IntMath.posmod_i(a, b)`, all with `b > 0` and correct for either sign of `a` (`floor_div(-7, 2)` is `-4`; `posmod_i(-7, 2)` is `1`; `ceil_div(-7, 2)` is `-3`). `b <= 0` is a caller defect: the helper returns 0 (never aborts: an aborted GDScript function returns a default the caller cannot tell from a result), and the debug-build `assert(b > 0)` fires in tests. ADR-0005 is the sole owner of the `IntMath` function list (`trunc_div`, `floor_div`, `ceil_div`, `posmod_i`, `lsr`, `low32`); ADR-0010 § 5.4 cites it and keeps only the file path and the single-annotation rule. Bodies: `trunc_div(a, b)` is `a / b` (the one annotated site); `floor_div(a, b)` is `trunc_div(a - posmod(a, b), b)` (exact, because `a - posmod(a, b)` is a multiple of `b`); `posmod_i(a, b)` is the global `posmod(a, b)` builtin, which returns an `int` for two ints (P5); `ceil_div(a, b)` is `floor_div(a + b - 1, b)`; each sits behind the `b <= 0` guard.
143:2. **There is no bare `/` or `%` anywhere else.** **The engine gate covers the binary `a / b` only** (P6, P19). `integer_division` at error level rejects `a / b` on two ints, but `c /= b` loads and runs, and no engine warning covers `%` or `%=`. The lexical rules close the holes: ADR-0010 `SIM-04` bans `%`, `/=` and `%=` outside `IntMath` (bad fixtures `x /= y` and `x %= y`; any `//`-style helper joins the ban), and `SIM-05` keeps exactly one `@warning_ignore("integer_division")` in `src/`, on the `return a / b` of `IntMath.trunc_div`. This ADR adopts that design instead of a marked bare form and supplies the semantics: `IntMath` exposes `trunc_div` (the engine's truncation, named when truncation is meant), `floor_div`, `ceil_div`, `posmod_i`, plus `lsr` and `low32`; none of the new helpers divides. The cost is measured (P14): the static `floor_div` costs about 12 times a bare operator (0.20 against 0.017 microseconds in a tight loop on the editor binary, re-measured). If S1 (SP-ENG-1) shows that cost matters in the Graph propagation or the Emitter exposure loop on a release export, the remedy (inlining a proven-non-negative form in named hot files) is an ADR-0010 amendment decided on that measurement, not an exception taken here.
146:The Suit "convention for negative operands" (ADR candidate 4, TR-suit-030) is therefore: floor for every quotient, `floor_div` / `posmod_i`; a thermal integrator that needs truncation toward zero calls `IntMath.trunc_div(a, b)` explicitly, which names the intent. Emitter `floor_div` (non-negative, checked) is a special case of the helper here and Emitter's lint fixtures stay valid.
243:The result is a **non-negative 63-bit `int`**, so every `mod` on it acts on a non-negative number. `Ihash.h32(...)` is `ihash(...) & 0xFFFFFFFF`. It is not a random stream: it has no counter and no state, it is never persisted, and it is used for variation that must be reproducible without being a persisted draw (Horror mark seeds, LURK waypoint rank and L3 timing with `HE_HASH_SEED` 0x4845; Attention beat jitter `h32(HASH_SEED, tell_epoch, k, 0, SALT_BEAT)`; Lighting gutter onset `H(emitter_id, k)`; Instruments tremor from `ref_key`). Rules: callers pick a fixed non-zero seed or salt (`mix64(0) = 0` makes `ihash(0, 0, 0, 0, 0)` equal 0); inputs are stable ids and indices, never `tick_alpha`, `present_time` or a frame count; each system keeps its own seed constant so changing one re-rolls only that system. Presentation may call it (it is pure); it must never call `DetRng.derive`. **A truth-channel visual that must be reproducible (the Failure & Trail's `trail.vis`) uses `Ihash` keyed by `world_seed` and a fixed per-system seed**: `Ihash.h(TRAIL_VIS_SEED, subject_id, stamp_index, world_seed, SALT_TRAIL_VIS)`, indexed by `IntMath.posmod_i(h, n)` for variant, phase and flip. The simulation never draws a `trail.vis` stream, so the hash reproduces the variant without opening the sim RNG API to presentation, and a different `world_seed` still changes at least one variant. `TRAIL_VIS_SEED` is a fixed non-zero constant the Trail GDD defines; its FT-20, D.6 and AC-134 stub vectors regenerate (sync item), and ADR-0009 line 137 changes to "reads `Ihash` keyed by `world_seed` (ADR-0005 § 2.6)". The alternative of letting presentation call the pure `DetRng.derive` for names ending `.vis` under a lint row was rejected. **Overflow waiver:** the Perception Filter's PF-37 "no dependence on integer overflow" wording is waived for the `Ihash` family, because 64-bit wrap is the pinned, golden-tested behaviour (deterministic on 4.7.2, P1; formally C++ undefined behaviour, guarded by the golden vectors and S0-b). This ADR chose the waiver plus ADR-0024's migration of PF D.14, with no separate masked variant. Presentation hashes use `Ihash` or `Ihash.h32` with a fixed non-zero per-system seed. Reference vectors (Python and GDScript agree): `ihash(0x4845, 1, 0, 0, 1)` = `0x2B1792AE18418A3E`; `ihash(0x4845, 17, 3, 5, 2)` = `0x31500F22473CCE18`; `ihash(0x4845, -1, -1, -1, 5)` = `0x0CA990E4614F7103`.

143:  - **`:=` is banned in `src/` and `tools/`** (`INFERRED_DECLARATION=2` makes every inferred declaration an error); every `var` and `const` has an explicit type. **Lambdas are fully typed**: `func(x: int) -> int:`, parameters and return.
219:- **Every `debug/gdscript/warnings/*` severity is 2 (error) except `RETURN_VALUE_DISCARDED`, which is 0.** No warning is left at 1, because a level-1 warning prints nothing headless (P10) and therefore cannot fail CI. ## Engine Compatibility

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Engine** | Godot 4.7.2 (stable, mono build probed), GDScript |
| **Domain** | Core (simulation state layout, integer arithmetic, serialization shape) |
| **Knowledge Risk** | MEDIUM. Everything this ADR uses predates 4.4 except typed `Dictionary[K, V]` (4.4), `@abstract` (4.5) and the two 4.7 GDScript rows in `breaking-changes.md`. The engine reference has no core or scripting module (`modules/` holds animation, audio, input, navigation, networking, physics, rendering and ui only), so packed-array semantics, integer behaviour and reflection are sourced from ADR-0005's probe table (P1 to P22) and from this ADR's own probes, and stay UNVERIFIED on a release export until spikes S0-a and S3 run there. |
| **References Consulted** | `docs/engine-reference/godot/VERSION.md`; `breaking-changes.md` (4.6 to 4.7 GDScript rows; 4.4 to 4.5 `duplicate_deep` row); `deprecated-apis.md` (untyped Array/Dictionary pattern; `duplicate()` for nested data replaced by `duplicate_deep()` since 4.5); `current-best-practices.md` (GDScript 4.7: typed-return override, packed-array element writes); ADR-0005 Engine Compatibility P1, P5, P7, P8, P9, P11, P12, P14, P17, P20, P22 (cited by number below). No `modules/*.md` applies. |
| **Post-Cutoff APIs Used** | `@abstract` (4.5) on the `RoomSource` port only (ADR-0010 § 3); nothing from 4.5 to 4.7 in the layout itself. Typed `Dictionary[int, int]` (4.4) appears in derived lookup caches only, never in a payload. The two 4.7 rows that bind this ADR: **(1)** "Packed array element writes no longer call the setter" (`breaking-changes.md`, `current-best-practices.md`): the Graph has no packed-array setters and marks every dirty key explicitly through `scope.mark_dirty` (§ 10); probed again below (P-d). **(2)** "Overrides inherit a typed return": binds anything that overrides a typed owner callable or an `@abstract` port method, so `RoomSource` implementers return on all paths (Implementation Guidelines). |
| **Verification Required** | Probed 2026-10-29 on `Godot_v4.7.2-stable_mono_win64_console.exe --headless --script` (editor binary, not a release export; scripts in `C:/Users/dasbl/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/adr-probes/0011/`): **(a)** the typed numeric builtins `mini`, `maxi`, `clampi`, `absi`, `signi` exist and return `int` for `int` arguments (3, 5, 5, 4, -1); **(b)** `get_property_list()` on a `RefCounted` subclass lists every script variable, underscore-prefixed ones included and in declaration order, selectable with `PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_VARIABLE` (the basis of the reflection test in § 6.3); **(c)** swapping two `PackedInt64Array` members by reference works and an alias taken before a member element write sees the write (ADR-0005 P7 reproduced); **(d)** `arr[i] = v` on a packed member runs no setter (P8 reproduced, and no setter is declared); **(e)** `PackedInt64Array.fill(0)` on 4096 elements costs 1.65 microseconds, `duplicate()` of 4096 elements 0.11 microseconds, and `duplicate()` followed by the first element write on 8192 `int32` elements 0.71 microseconds (`duplicate()` shares the buffer until the first write on either side; the copy is paid by the next mutator's first write, § Performance); **(f)** a typed `Dictionary[int, int]` answers `get(k, -1)`; **(g)** `PackedInt32Array` stores wrap to 32 bits (`3000000000` reads `-1294967296`, ADR-0005 P9) and `PackedByteArray` to 8 bits (`300` reads `44`); **(h)** `var_to_bytes` returns a `StringName` dictionary key as a `StringName` (type 21) and a `String` key as a `String` (type 4), which is why payload keys must be `String` (ADR-0006 § 1.2 walk rejects `StringName`); **(i)** a synthetic zero-filled payload with this ADR's columns measures 29,674 canonical TLV bytes (29,560 `var_to_bytes` bytes) for 105 nodes, 150 edges, 270 ports, 14 compartments, 1 seam, 3 sections and 2 queued entries per queue, and 33,144 bytes at 120 nodes and 172 edges (value-independent, so a real save differs by at most the key-text length). **Still open and named:** S0-a and S0-b on a `template_release` export (Windows, Linux x86-64, Linux arm64 / Deck) for items (c), (d), (e) and (g); S1 (SP-ENG-1) for GDScript accessor, `Callable.call` and `IntMath.floor_div` cost in the real phases; S3 (snapshot, restore and `post_restore` time and size on the F-MVP fixture on RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK); LINT-SPIKE-1 for loading every Key Interfaces snippet under the ADR-0010 § 5.1 warning configuration (the snippets here follow its typing rules but have not been load-checked). |

=====
### 6. Persisted, derived, scratch, diagnostic

**6.1 Store extensive, derive intensive** (LS-1 (c), TR-lsg-004). Persisted: the extensive quantities and the hysteresis memory. Derived: everything a pure function of persisted state, the catalog and Layout.

| Class | Members |
|---|---|
| **PERSISTED** (`GraphState`) | `n_o2`, `n_inert`, `t`, `t_rem`, `fuel_puddle`; `stock`, `tc_rem`, `t_cool`, `fuel_rem`, `out_w`; `hp`, `hp_cap`, `state`, `forced_mode`, `forced_next`; the six step stamps and `mode_key`; `thaw_until`; the band memory `band_o2/p/t`, `p_prev`, the warn trackers `warn_o2/p/t`, `warn_bits`; the two STRAIN bits per stored OPENING; `req`, breaker, valve `open`, `area`, `capped`, `open_end`; the section counters; the `pending_*` and `draw_grant` queues; the id counters, `last_step_*`, the def table |
| **DERIVED** (`GraphCaches`) | `P`, `p_o2`, `o2_pm`, `pressure_trend`; `V`, `exposed_tiles`; `served_pm`, `circ`, `run_pm`; components, trees, `path_cap`, degrees, adjacency CSR, the `power_use` window; the failure-descriptor store; last-emitted dirty buckets; id-to-slot maps and endpoint slots; the def-row and `def_waste_pm` columns; `topology_version`, `topo_dirty`, lifecycle (`EMPTY`/`LIVE`) |
| **SCRATCH** (`GraphScratch`) | per-phase buffers sized by structural mutators: the Jacobi `next` columns (§ 6.2) and the accumulators and flux arrays ADR-0012 declares |
| **DIAGNOSTIC** (`GraphDiag`) | `saturations` (indexed by a `SatField` enum), `stale_calls`, `gate_holds`, `stall_edges`, `footprints_dropped`, `stock_clamped`, `hash_invocations` |

`P`, `p_o2` and `served_pm` are recomputed at the end of their phase and in `post_restore`, and a read returns the cached value, so `read_view` stays pure (TR-lsg-018) and the first presented frame after a restore is correct (the GDD has `post_restore` derive `served_pm` and the descriptor list from restored state).

**6.2 Aliasing and the Jacobi pair.** S0-a, the packed-array aliasing question the GDD left open, is **closed for the data model by ADR-0005 P7 and probes (c), (d)**: a `Packed*Array` is shared by reference by assignment, by argument and by a getter, an element write through any alias is visible through all, and only `duplicate()` isolates (by deferred copy-on-write, probe (e)). Consequences, as rules: **(1)** a function may take a local alias of a column for reads and writes within one phase (no one resizes during a phase); **(2)** an alias is never kept across a kernel call, a `snapshot`, a `restore` or a structural mutator (`resize` and member re-assignment would orphan it); **(3)** a snapshot is never a local alias: it is a `duplicate()` placed in the payload (ADR-0003); **(4)** Jacobi's "start-of-phase snapshot" is two member arrays, the `GraphState` column and a `GraphScratch` `next` array of the same length, swapped by reference at the phase end (`var t: PackedInt64Array = state_col; state_col = scratch_next; scratch_next = t`, allocation-free, probe (c)). Which columns are double-buffered and when the swap happens is ADR-0012's; the data model's contribution is that `next` arrays live in `GraphScratch`, are sized with the table, and that anything holding a column reference reads it through the member each time (the `GraphView` facade reads `state` members, never a cached array), so a swap cannot strand a reader.

**6.3 The persisted-field check (TR-lsg-038).** Two CI checks, both in `tests/unit/graph/`:
- **Method A, reflection.** Enumerate `GraphState.new().get_property_list()` filtered by `PROPERTY_USAGE_SCRIPT_VARIABLE` (probed: includes underscore members, in declaration order). Every name must be either a column that `GraphSnapshot.build()` writes into the payload (the check builds a payload from a populated state and compares the key sets against `GraphSchema`) or one of the three holder references `_caches`, `_scratch`, `_diag`. The same enumeration over `GraphCaches` and `GraphScratch` compares against the checked-in allowlist `tests/fixtures/graph/derived_members.json` (one entry per member: reason and rebuilding function), which fails on any member not listed and on any listed member that does not exist.
- **Method B, zero and diff.** For each `GraphCaches` member, zero it (or `reset()` the cache) in a copy of a mid-fault state, run one step, and assert the copy's `state_hash` equals the unmodified control's after `ensure_derived()` has been allowed to run; a step that reads a cache it did not first recompute shows as a differing hash. `GraphScratch` members are cleared the same way. Both must pass.

**6.4 Conservation (TR-lsg-005).** The sixteen section counters of § 3.7 are the persisted half of LS-1 (e). `src/shared/graph/graph_invariants.gd` holds pure evaluators over a `GraphState`, read only: `gas_total(state, section_id)`, `heat_total_mdj(state, section_id)`, `coolant_total(state, section_id)`, `fuel_total_uml(state, section_id)`, each the left side of the LS-1 (e) equality for that medium (gas: `n_o2 + n_inert` over compartments, plus O2_TANK stock, plus `vented_mgu`, `breathed_mgu`, `disc_mgu` and `wd_mgu`, minus `produced_mgu`; heat in milli-dJ over compartments' `T x C + t_rem` and every RESERVOIR's heat store, plus `1000 x (radiated_dj - produced_dj)` and `spilled_heat_mdj`; coolant and fuel as LS-1 (e) gives, fuel in micro-mL with `fuel_rem` subtracted). **A test asserts each total equals its value at the section's instantiation after every step of every fixture, on a running ship with sources, sinks and crew active.** The baseline is held by the test (it is a function of the template), not persisted, which keeps the LS-21 field list unchanged. The exact term lists stay in the GDD; the evaluators are the executable form and are what a reviewer diffs against LS-1 (e).

**6.5 Perception independence (TR-lsg-018).** `src/sim/graph/**` imports nothing from `src/presentation/` (`ARCH-02`), names none of `PERCEPTION_OUT`, `perceived(`, `PerceptionRef` (ADR-0010 `READ-03` token list for the directory), and requests no `PERCEPTION_OUT` view; a mutator argument is an id, a magnitude, an enum or a plan (LS-22). The fixture of LS-22 (a degraded ship with and without a Perception block set to "all OK") asserts the `state_hash` of `graph.state` is identical.

**D3.1 One hook.** `HookDescriptor{hook_id &"emitter.place", divisor 1, offset 0, after [{id &"body.integrate", tolerates_stale false}, {id &"graph.propagate.failure", tolerates_stale true}]}`. `body.integrate` runs every tick (the hooks coincide), so its edge is not stale-tolerant; the failure hook runs once per `GRAPH_STEP_TICKS`, so its edge declares `tolerates_stale` (ADR-0003 guideline). Because the compiled order is global, `emitter.place` is after the power and atmo hooks on every tick on which they run, and after `controller.step` and `layout.doors` through `body.integrate` (ADR-0014 section 7, same-tick truth). In MIRROR mode the hook is not run (ADR-0001) and a replica reads the replicated `SHARED_SUMMARY`; what that summary carries is a VS-B ask recorded in Open Questions, not decided here. No second Emitter hook exists in the MVP.
====
**D6.4 Fault glow: derived, reconciled once per completed Graph step, never in `post_restore` (TR-emitter-027, TR-ftrail-041; answers ADR-0012 Open Question 3).** FAULT_GLOW rows are canonical (they carry `glow_key`, `sev`, `placed_tick`), so a restore restores them; they are created and removed by W1 and by nothing else. W1 reconciles **iff `GraphView.last_step_no() != hdr.fault_step_seen`**, that is, once for each Graph step the failure hook has completed, on the tick after its phase 11 ran (the hook is `after: graph.propagate.failure`, so it reads that step's final descriptor store), and then writes `fault_step_seen = last_step_no`. `post_restore` does not reconcile and does not touch the rows. Consequences: in the uninterrupted run and in the restored run the reconciliation happens at the same ticks against a descriptor store freshly produced by the same phase 11, so the one-step window ADR-0012 section 11 leaves in the *store* between a restore and the next phase 11 is never read by the Emitter; the glow of a descriptor appears on the failure tick of the step in which it appears, never later (EM-1). Reconciliation reads `GraphView.failures(filter, out)` with a reusable `FailureFilter` (`loaded_only`, `min_sev` from the glow table) and compares it, in ascending descriptor id, with the existing FAULT_GLOW rows keyed by `glow_key`: new descriptors with a glow row (`GlowTable`, keyed by `(mode, medium)`) create a row, vanished ones remove it, `sev` changes update `sev` (and the derived output `IntMath.floor_div(GLOW_BASE_PM[key] * SEV_GLOW_PM[sev], 1000)`), subject to `sev >= sev_min[key]` and output above zero. Position, section and frame: `section_id = GraphView.section_of(anchor)`, `anchor_px` = the head point `base_px_polyline[0]` of `LayoutView.anchor_geometry(anchor)` read once at creation (a cold read; an empty answer for a discarded section creates no row, counts `emitter_fault_glow_no_anchor` and retries at the next step), and `body_id` derived. CONCERNS (engine seat, Godot 4.7.2). One blocking finding (E1), a trivial snippet fix. The design is idiomatic for 4.7.2 and uses no deprecated or post-cutoff API.

Checks that came out clean:
- No `const` holds a constructed object. Only int constants appear (`RNG_*`, `HOOK_*`).
- The 4.7 typed-return override rule does not apply: the hooks are bound `Callable`s, not overrides.
- The 4.7 rule that packed-array element writes skip setters is harmless, because the Graph declares no setters.
  - Probe on 4.7.2: `h.col[1] = 9` ran 0 setter calls; whole-array assignment ran 1.
- Packed-array aliasing behaves as ADR-0011 § 6.2 states.
  - A local alias sees member element writes.
  - `duplicate()` isolates a snapshot from later member writes.
  - `resize` on the member also resizes the alias, because they share one ref.
  - Reassigning the member orphans the alias.

findings.text: The PhaseExchange excerpt contradicts the ADR's own § 2 rule (alias a column in a local for the phase) and the probe basis for the quoted costs. findings.text: The `pending_draw` sort key `(cid << 24) | (crew << 8) | arrival_index` gives arrival_index 8 bits, but the queue bound in § 5 and ADR-0011 § 3.8 is `MAX_CREW x compartment count`. findings.amendment: In the excerpt take locals before the loop (`var n_o2: PackedInt64Array = s.n_o2`, `var n_inert: PackedInt64Array = s.n_inert`, `var va: PackedInt32Array = c.comp_v`, and so on) and compute `n_o2[ra] + n_inert[ra]` inline instead of `s._c_n_total_at(...)`. Add one sentence to § 13.1 and Performance Implications: 'probes (d) to (f) are local-array costs; member access measured about 64 ns per element and a method or static call about 120 ns on the editor binary; S1 decides'. If a helper is kept, give it a public name and list it in ADR-0011's GraphState interface.

findings.text: The `pending_draw` sort key `(cid << 24) | (crew << 8) | arrival_index` gives arrival_index 8 bits, but the queue bound in § 5 and ADR-0011 § 3.8 is `MAX_CREW x compartment count`. That is 4 x 14 = 56 at MVP but 4 x about 120 = 480 in VS-A, more if a caller enqueues once per tick (6 per step). An arrival_index of 256 or more carries into the crew field. GDScript int64 never faults, so the (compartment, crew) order claimed in § 5 is silently corrupted, and the grant between two crew in a thin room becomes order-dependent. The trace key `(subject_ref << 16) | (kind << 8) | arrival_index` is safe at the 16-entry bound.
findings.amendment: Widen the draw key to `(cid << 32) | (crew << 16) | arrival_index` (all three fields are far below 2^31 and 2^16), or keep the layout and add a `GRAPH_BOOT_TUNING` check that the bound is at most 255. State the bit widths in the § 5 text and in the HOT-01 and unit-test fixtures.

findings.text: Probe (c) timed a `while` insertion sort, but PROP-01 (Foundation Ask 3) bans `while` in propagate/ and § 3 mandates 'a bounded `for` with `break`'. The probed form is therefore not the shipped form. I re-timed the `for j: ... in range(i-1,-1,-1)` + `break` form on random keys: 3.5, 27.0 and 33.3 µs at 16, 56 and 64 entries (not slower than the `while` form). On reverse-sorted input at 64 entries it is 55.3 µs. The text 'at most 43 microseconds at the 64-entry bound' (Performance Implications) is a random-input figure, not a bound. The probe's 64 is also well below the VS-A queue bound (see E4).
findings.amendment: Replace probe (c) with the `for`+`break` form and quote the reverse-sorted worst case (about 55 µs on the editor binary) as the bound. Keep the random-input figure as typical.

findings.text: § 1 says 'the kernel never drops a tick at LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS 0, and a longer stall delays ticks without skipping them'. ADR-0001's forgiveness rule does drop whole lag ticks of wall time after the per-frame cap (`dropped = lag_ticks, acc <- acc mod TICK_UNITS`). What is true, and what the Graph relies on, is that the tick counter T stays gapless, so `T mod 6` hooks always run on consecutive ticks and a step is never skipped. The sentence as written is ambiguous.
findings.amendment: Reword to: 'the kernel may forgive lag (drop accumulated wall time, ADR-0001), but T is gapless, so no hook due on T is skipped and a step is never skipped or repeated; a cursor gap arises only from a refused or faulted hook or a restore.'

cross_adr.text: ADR-0012 § 1 states the kernel 'never drops a tick' at LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS 0. ADR-0001 (frame body, forgiveness) drops whole lag ticks of wall time (`dropped = lag_ticks; acc <- acc mod TICK_UNITS`). The tick counter T itself stays gapless, which is what the Graph needs. This is a wording inconsistency, not a design conflict.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0012 rewords § 1 as in E6. ADR-0001 should state in one sentence that T is gapless under forgiveness and that hooks keyed on `T mod C` are therefore never skipped.

cross_adr.text: ADR-0011 § 6.2 (4) prescribes `next` columns swapped by reference. ADR-0012 § 3 replaces that with int64 accumulators in GraphScratch. The engine facts support the change: the swap strands aliases, and a member reassignment orphans a local alias (probed). ADR-0011's writer-set guideline also says scratch is written only in `graph_propagate.gd`, while ADR-0012 uses the whole `propagate/` directory. ADR-0011 does not declare any total-amount accessor such as the `_c_n_total_at` that ADR-0012's excerpt calls.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0011 amends § 6.2 (4) to 'accumulators only', lists the accumulator members (PackedInt64Array) and the directory writer set, and either declares a public total-amount helper on GraphState or drops the need for one (E3).

cross_adr.text: ADR-0010 LINT-SPIKE-1(a) leaves open whether `can_instantiate()` is true for a static-only class such as IntMath. On 4.7.2 (probe 2026-10-29, scratch project with warnings at 2) it is true for static-only `class_name X extends RefCounted` scripts (IntMath, GraphRules) and for stub RefCounted classes. A script that fails a promoted warning returned a non-null script and the editor logged 'Parse Error ... (Warning treated as error.)', as in ADR-0010 P3. ADR-0012's PhaseExchange and GraphRules rely on the static-only form.
cross_adr.amendment: ADR-0010 records this outcome in § 1.2 and closes the static-only half of LINT-SPIKE-1(a). Abstract ports remain open. No change is needed to ADR-0012 beyond E1.
